task_instance: Write an EAS Workflows YAML file (.eas/workflows/build-and-submit.yml) for a minimal sample Expo project that builds iOS and Android production builds on push to main and submits the iOS build, then validate it per the skill's required 'npx eas-cli workflow:validate' step.
blocker_detail: The skill mandates validating any generated/edited workflow file with `npx -y eas-cli@latest workflow:validate .eas/workflows/<file>.yml --non-interactive` and treats this as the authoritative validator (explicitly says not to substitute a local YAML/JSON-Schema validator). Running this against the sample project produced: 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Error: Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable...'. EAS CLI validation also requires a linked Expo project (real project id, not the placeholder used here) and, for build/submit jobs, paid Apple Developer/Google Play accounts as the skill's own header warns. Logging in or supplying an EXPO_TOKEN is an account-bound/credentialed action forbidden by the sandbox rules, so the deliverable could not be verified as the skill requires. Separately, the skill's first mandatory step (fetch the JSON Schema from https://api.expo.dev/v2/workflows/schema) was also blocked: the sandbox's egress proxy returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' / 'connect_rejected (organization policy)' for api.expo.dev, while raw.githubusercontent.com (used for the syntax/pre-packaged-jobs docs) was reachable. So even the schema-fetch prerequisite is not available in this runtime, independent of the login requirement.
evidence: Commands run: `curl -sS https://api.expo.dev/v2/workflows/schema` -> exit 56, CONNECT tunnel failed 403 (agent proxy denied api.expo.dev by organization policy; confirmed via /__agentproxy/status recentRelayFailures pattern for other blocked hosts). `curl -sS https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../syntax.mdx` -> HTTP 200 (docs fetch works). Built sample project files: /tmp/.../expo__skills__eas-workflows/package.json, app.json, eas.json, and the workflow file /tmp/.../expo__skills__eas-workflows/.eas/workflows/build-and-submit.yml (name/on.push/jobs with build_ios, build_android, submit_ios using needs and ${{ needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id }} expression syntax, following the fetched syntax.mdx reference since the JSON Schema itself was unreachable). Ran `npx -y eas-cli@latest --version` -> eas-cli/24.8.0 installed successfully (npm registry reachable). Ran `npx -y eas-cli@latest workflow:validate .eas/workflows/build-and-submit.yml --non-interactive` -> output: 'An Expo user account is required to proceed.' / 'Error: Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable if you're using EAS CLI on CI'. Per sandbox safety rules, credentials/account login for a paid, account-bound service (EAS) may not be used, so the mandated validation step could not be completed and the deliverable (a validated EAS workflow YAML) could not be verified.
